update.title: Made Modular Flow Engine callable over HTTP
update.summary: Added a FastAPI service for inspecting, validating, and executing JSON flows, while sink-owned return, file, and console destinations define how completed results are delivered.

blocks.body:
## Expose the engine as a service

Modular Flow Engine now exposes the same JSON flows through a FastAPI service. Clients can list available flows, inspect their inputs and components, validate a request, execute a flow, and check service health without importing engine internals or spawning the CLI themselves.

The CLI and HTTP service use the same execution engine, so a flow remains one portable document rather than gaining a separate server-specific format.

blocks.caption: The flow’s sink configuration determines both result delivery and the service’s default wait behavior.
blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  Request[HTTP execute request] --> Check{Return destination?}
  Check -->|Yes| Wait[Wait for result]
  Check -->|No| Accept[Accept background run]
  Wait --> Engine[Shared flow engine]
  Accept --> Engine
  Engine --> Sink{Declared sink destinations}
  Sink --> Return[API response]
  Sink --> File[JSON file]
  Sink --> Console[Console output]
blocks.summary: The flow’s sink configuration determines both result delivery and the service’s default wait behavior.

blocks.body:
## Let sinks define where results go

Each collector or JSON writer names one or more destinations for its finalized value. `return` adds data to the HTTP response, `file` writes JSON beneath the run’s output directory, and `console` prints it for command-line use. The execution context owns these writers, so sinks share one delivery contract and nested flow scopes can contribute to one response.

The service inspects those declarations before execution. A flow with a `return` destination waits and sends the collected value back; a file- or console-only flow is accepted for background execution. Callers can override the default wait behavior explicitly.

blocks.caption: One sink can return its completed value to the caller and write the same result to a file.
